title: Peasant Movements Champaran Satyagraha
definition: The 1917 Champaran Satyagraha was the first civil disobedience movement in India led by Mahatma Gandhi, aimed at ending the exploitative 'Tinkathia' system imposed by European indigo planters on the peasantry of Bihar.
importanceInUpsc: It marks the transition of the Indian National Movement from elite-led constitutional agitation to mass-based Gandhian struggle, frequently tested for its methodology and socio-economic impact.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Peasant Movements Champaran Satyagraha.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Core foundational concepts of Gandhian ideology
Understanding of British Land Revenue Systems
